text:
In the Kingdom of Echoes, citizens paid their debts not with coins, but with forgotten things. The baker gave away his childhood lullaby; the blacksmith surrendered the scent of his first forge. In return, they received smooth, gray stones from the Royal Vault. These stones were empty vessels, meant to hold new memories.

Young Elara, desperate for warmth in her drafty cottage, traded the memory of her mother’s laughter for a heavy, obsidian stone. She placed it by her fire, hoping it would radiate heat. Instead, it absorbed every flicker of flame, leaving her shivering in darkness.

Desperate, she wandered into the Whispering Woods, where an old fox sat atop a pile of discarded stones. “Why do you hoard emptiness?” Elara asked.

The fox tilted its head. “I don’t hoard. I remember.” He nudged a pale blue stone toward her. Inside it glowed a faint, golden light—the exact shade of Elara’s lost laughter. “Generosity,” the fox whispered, “is the act of giving your past away so someone else can carry it. But the universe keeps a receipt. What you give freely returns, changed by the hands that held it.”

Elara took the stone. It was cold, yet when she hugged it, she felt the warmth of being remembered.
